title: Evaluation of an AND-node and its CNF
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $cs$ be a list of normal-form OR circuits on $n$ variables, and let $x$ be an assignment of Boolean values to those variables. Suppose every member of $cs$ is a base OR-clause, given by a list of circuit literals and a witness that their variable indices are pairwise distinct. The AND-node over $cs$ and the CNF obtained from that node have the same value on $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $cs$ is a list of normal-form OR circuits on $n$ variables
$x$ assigns a Boolean value to each of the $n$ variables
Every member of $cs$ is a base OR-clause
replaced:
Let $cs$ be a list of normal-form OR circuits on $n$ variables, and suppose that every
entry of $cs$ is an OR-clause — that is, a base clause given by a list of literals,
rather than an internal OR node. Then for every assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to
\bbf_2$, evaluating the normal-form AND circuit that conjoins the circuits in $cs$
agrees with evaluating the CNF formula built from it: the value at $x$ of the AND-node
over $cs$ equals the value at $x$ of the CNF whose clauses are obtained by converting
each OR-clause of $cs$ into a disjunction of literals.
